h1:
First Time in Lampang
What to Know + a 2-Day, 1-Night Plan
intro: Lampang is a northern town you can take slowly all day. Real horse carriages still trot down the streets, old Lanna temples sit quietly around town, and the riverside old quarter along the Wang River is still very much alive. If it's your first visit and you're not sure where to start, here's what to know before you go — from how to get there, to where to stay, to a 2-day, 1-night plan that works well for newcomers.

blocks.html: Lampang isn't a town you need to rush. First-time visitors are often surprised at how quiet and walkable it is. The good stuff sits close together — old temples, the old-town market, riverside cafés, and the charm of horse carriages that still run as part of everyday life, not just as a tourist show. Reading through these basics first will make your first trip go a lot more smoothly.

Lampang is reachable by train, bus and plane — pick whatever suits your budget and time. A favourite is the northern train line, partly for the scenery and partly because Lampang's own station is a lovely old wooden building that's worth a photo.

items: By plane — direct flights from Bangkok (Don Mueang) land at Lampang Airport in about 1 hour. There are only a few flights a day, so book ahead for the best fares.
By train — from Bangkok on the northern line it's a long ride (you can take an overnight sleeper). From Chiang Mai it's only about 2 hours, and the stretch through Khun Tan is gorgeous.

By bus / minivan — from Bangkok (Mo Chit) several operators run all day. From Chiang Mai there's Green Bus and the route 152 minivans leaving frequently every 20–30 minutes, with fares in the low hundreds of THB.
By car — about 100 km from Chiang Mai, roughly 1.5 hours. Handy if you want to detour to temples outside town and out to Chae Son.

blocks.title: First-Timer Tip
blocks.html: If you're coming from Chiang Mai and want to skip driving, the Chiang Mai–Lampang train is fun and cheap, usually under 100 THB. Get off at the station and grab a horse carriage or a ride into town from there.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Lampang trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Lampang
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: Lampang is a small town, and the main sights cluster along the Wang River and the old quarter. Staying within walking distance of Kad Kong Ta is the most convenient choice.

items.name: Kad Kong Ta / Wang Riverside
items.blurb: The heart of the old town — walking distance to the night-market street, riverside cafés and Ratsadaphisek Bridge. Great for first-timers who'd rather not drive.

items.name: City Centre / Boonyawat Road
items.blurb: Close to restaurants, markets and breakfast spots, with a range of room prices and easy access to rides.

items.name: Out-of-Town Resorts / Chae Son
items.blurb: Good if you're after nature, hot springs and cooler air — but you'll need a car, since it's a fair way from town.

blocks.text: What to See First — the Big Ones You Shouldn't Miss

items.name: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
items.blurb: An ancient Lanna temple on a low hill outside town with stunning architecture. The highlight is the upside-down reflection of the chedi inside a darkened viharn — people line up to see it. If there's one temple that defines Lampang, this is it.
items.meta: Ko Kha district · about 18 km from town · open morning–evening

items.name: Kad Kong Ta (Walking Street)
items.blurb: The old riverside quarter along the Wang, lined with wooden shophouses and mixed-style old buildings. It turns into a walking street on Saturday and Sunday evenings, with food, cafés and crafts — best around sunset.

items.name: A Horse-Carriage Ride Around Town
items.blurb: Lampang is the only town in Thailand where horse carriages still run for real. There are pickup stands around town, and it's a relaxed way to see the riverside old quarter and its temples. Always agree on the price with the driver before you climb aboard.
items.meta: Several routes · from about ฿150 for a short loop

items.name: Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat Phra Chomklao Rachanusorn (Doi Phra Bat)
items.blurb: White chedis scattered across a limestone peak, with sweeping views that feel almost otherworldly. You have to take a local truck up, and it's still a photo spot that not everyone has reached.
items.meta: Chae Hom district · transfer truck required to the top

items.name: Thai Elephant Conservation Center
items.blurb: A government-run elephant care centre with elephant painting shows and learning activities about elephants — good for families and kids. It sits along the Lampang–Lamphun road.
items.meta: Hang Chat district · opens in the morning, shows at set times

items.name: Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao Suchadaram
items.blurb: An old in-town temple that once housed the Emerald Buddha. The chedi and viharn show a handsome mix of Lanna and Burmese styles, and it's an easy stroll from the town centre.

items.name: Baan Sao Nak
items.blurb: A century-old teak house, now open as a small museum, that shows how Lampang's wealthy families once lived. It's quiet, peaceful and very photogenic.
items.meta: In the old town · small entry fee

items.name: Chae Son National Park
items.blurb: Natural hot springs where you can soak your feet and boil eggs, alongside a waterfall and cool air. Worth it if you have an extra day and a car — it's about 1.5 hours from town.
items.meta: Mueang Pan district · far from town, car needed

blocks.html: This plan is built for first-timers with no need to rush, focusing on the main in-town sights and the key temple just outside town that isn't too far. With no car of your own, you can call a ride or hire a local truck for the temple runs outside town.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Old Town, Horse Carriages and Kad Kong Ta

items.activity: Start the morning with a Lampang-style breakfast
items.note: Rice porridge, old-school coffee, or khao soi / khanom jeen nam ngiao in town. Fuel up before you wander.

items.activity: Temple walk in town — Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao and the riverside temples
items.note: Stroll at an easy pace and take in the mixed Lanna–Burmese architecture while the morning sun is still soft.
Agree on the price with the driver first. Short loops start around ฿150 and roll through the old quarter along the Wang River.

items.activity: Lunch at a northern Thai restaurant in town
items.note: Try nam prik num with crispy pork rinds, or a well-known spot near Kad Kong Ta.

items.activity: Café break by the Wang River
items.note: The Ratsadaphisek Bridge area has several riverside cafés — a nice place to dodge the afternoon heat.

items.activity: Walk Kad Kong Ta (if it's a Saturday or Sunday)
items.note: The walking street runs from evening until around 22:00 with food, crafts and old-building photo ops. On weekdays you can still wander the quarter for the architecture.

items.activity: Dinner — moo kratha or a riverside spot
items.note: Lampang has plenty of moo kratha (DIY grill-hotpot) buffets, popular with locals.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Lanna Temple Outside Town + Souvenirs Before Heading Home

items.activity: Head out of town to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
items.note: It's in Ko Kha district, about 18 km away. Go early while crowds are thin and the light is lovely.

items.activity: See Wat Phra That Lampang Luang and the upside-down chedi reflection
items.note: Step into the darkened viharn to see the inverted chedi projected through a small opening — an unmissable highlight.
Lampang's famous rooster-bowl ceramic museum — watch the pieces being made and pick up ceramic souvenirs.

items.activity: Lunch on the way back into town
items.note: Noodles or a local eatery along the road.

items.activity: Souvenir shopping — khao tan, ceramics, crispy pork
items.note: Watermelon-glazed khao tan rice crackers and rooster bowls are the town's signature take-home gifts.

items.activity: One last café or photo stop before you go
items.note: The old wooden Lampang train station is a great photo spot before you catch your ride home.

blocks.title: Adjust the Plan
blocks.html: With 3 days, add a nature day out to Chae Son to soak in the hot springs, or head up to Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat (Doi Phra Bat) for photos of the white chedis. Travelling with kids? You can swap the Thai Elephant Conservation Center into Day 2 for the morning.

blocks.text: Good to Know Before You Go

items: Kad Kong Ta is open Saturday–Sunday — if you want the full walking-street experience, plan your trip over a weekend. On weekdays you can still walk the quarter for the old buildings, but there are fewer stalls.

Many sights are outside town — Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, the elephant centre and Chae Son all need a car. If you're not driving, hiring a local truck or arranging a ride by the trip works out better.
Agree on horse-carriage prices first — there are several routes at different prices, so confirm with the driver before you get on to avoid confusion at the end.
Best time to visit — November to February is cool and pleasant for walking around. March to April can bring haze to the north, so check the air quality before you go.
This is a slow town — many places close early, and breakfast dishes and khao soi often sell out before afternoon, so plan your morning meal.

faq.q: First time in Lampang — how many days is enough?
faq.a: Two days and one night is about right for first-timers. You can cover the main in-town sights, the horse carriages, Kad Kong Ta and Wat Phra That Lampang Luang outside town. If you want to add nature like Chae Son or Doi Phra Bat, stretching it to 3 days and 2 nights is more comfortable.

faq.q: Can I visit Lampang without my own car?
faq.a: Yes. In town you can walk, take a horse carriage or call a ride. For temples and sights outside town, like Wat Phra That Lampang Luang and the elephant centre, it's best to hire a local truck by the trip — that's cheaper and easier than booking rides one at a time.

faq.q: What days and hours is Kad Kong Ta open?
faq.a: Kad Kong Ta runs as a walking street on Saturday and Sunday evenings, roughly 16:00–22:00, with food, cafés and crafts. On weekdays you can still stroll the quarter to see the old buildings, but there are fewer shops and stalls.

faq.q: How much is a Lampang horse-carriage ride?
faq.a: It depends on the route and distance. A short loop in town starts at around 150 THB, while a longer city tour costs more. Always confirm the price clearly with the driver before you get on.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Lampang?
faq.a: November through February is cool and the most pleasant for walking around. March to April can bring haze to the north from crop burning, so check the air quality before you plan.
